expected_text_segments:
EIA oil inventories: the sharper squeeze is in distillates

Why it matters: The U.S. Energy Information Administration's 4 November 2026 petroleum report puts the clearest sign of fuel-stock tightness in distillates.

Context: For the week ending 30 October, distillate inventories fell 3.6 million barrels and stood 13% below their five-year average.

Read the full brief: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/eia-oil-inventories-the-sharper-squeeze

Analysis, not financial advice.

Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.

media_manifest.alt_text: Horizontal bars show crude inventories 4% below their five-year average, gasoline 2% below and distillate 13% below for the week ending 30 October 2026. All bars share a percentage scale and zero reference.
media_manifest.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration · 4 Nov 2026 report, week ending 30 Oct. Independent chart: Capital Chronicle.
media_manifest.caption: EIA reported inventories 4% below their five-year average for crude excluding SPR, 2% below for gasoline and 13% below for distillate. This is a percentage comparison, not a barrel-volume comparison. Sources: [U.S. Energy Information Administration · 04 Nov 2026](https://ir.eia.gov/secure/wpsr/summary.txt).
media_manifest.placement_after: The sharper squeeze is in distillates
